<!--
  Instructions for people adding ParamBot rules. This belongs on the wiki at
  [[User:ParamBot/Rules/Instructions]], transcluded at the top of
  [[User:ParamBot/Rules]] with {{User:ParamBot/Rules/Instructions}}.

  Every <syntaxhighlight> example here is checked by tests/test_docs.py and
  must be valid. Never put an example rules table outside <syntaxhighlight>:
  on the rules page the bot would obey it.
-->
[[User:ParamBot|ParamBot]] reads this page to find out which template parameters to fix.

When a template stops accepting an old parameter name (for example {{tl|Infobox settlement}} replacing {{para|imagesize}} with {{para|image_size}}), a revert can put the old name back into an article. The infobox then silently drops that information and the article shows up in the template's "unknown parameters" category. Once a day, ParamBot checks those categories and renames the old parameters to the new ones. It changes nothing else.

'''Only add renames that already have consensus.''' Usually that means the template's deprecated-parameter check listed them.

== Adding a template ==
Each template gets a table, with the old parameter names on the left and the new names on the right.

# Edit this page. At the bottom, add a heading with the template's name.
# Copy the example table below and paste it under your heading.
# In the caption line (the one starting <code>|+</code>), change the template's name to yours.
# Change the rows so that each one holds an old name and its new name. Each row starts with a <code>|-</code> line; add one row per old name.
# Save.

<syntaxhighlight lang="wikitext">
== Infobox settlement ==
{| class="wikitable"
|+ {{tl|Infobox settlement}}
! Old parameter !! New parameter
|-
| {{para|settlement_type}} || {{para|type}}
|-
| {{para|imagesize}} || {{para|image_size}}
|-
| {{para|image_caption}} || {{para|caption}}
|}
</syntaxhighlight>

On the page, this shows as an ordinary table.

'''Already have the list in a table?''' If the renames are already in a wikitable, for example on the template's talk page, paste that table as it is. Then add a caption line straight after the <code>{|</code> line: <code><nowiki>|+ {{tl|Template name}}</nowiki></code>. The first column must hold the old names and the second the new ones. Any other columns are notes, unless one is headed ''If both are set'' ([[#If both parameters are filled in|see below]]).

'''Does the template still have a deprecated-parameter block?''' The bot operator can turn it into a table for you. Ask on [[User talk:ParamBot]].

'''Is the template already on this page?''' Add rows to its table instead of starting another one.

You don't have to wait until the template drops the old names. A rule does nothing while the template still accepts its old name, and starts working by itself once that name is removed.

== Writing rows ==
* '''Old name on the left, new name on the right.'''
* Write each name as {{tlx|para|name}}. Anything else in the cell is a note, which the bot ignores, such as <code><nowiki>{{para|spouse}} (will use {{tl|pluralize from text}})</nowiki></code>.
* Copy names exactly. Capital letters matter: {{para|Imagesize}} and {{para|imagesize}} are different parameters. Spaces are fine, for example {{para|honorific prefix}}.
* '''Numbered parameters:''' put <code>#</code> where the number goes, in both names. Two numbers work too, as in {{para|blank#_name_sec#}} → {{para|custom_label#_sec#}}.
* '''Parameters with no replacement:''' write <code>remove</code> in the new-name column. If one of these comes back, the bot deletes it and its value.
* '''Several old names with the same new name''' can each have a row, share a row (<code><nowiki>{{para|alma_mater}} {{para|alma mater}}</nowiki></code>), or share one new-name cell using <code>rowspan</code>.
* You don't need extra rows for redirects to the template. The bot finds them itself.

<syntaxhighlight lang="wikitext">
{| class="wikitable"
|+ {{tl|Infobox officeholder}}
! Old parameter !! New parameter
|-
| {{para|termstart#}} || {{para|term_start#}}
|-
| {{para|spouse(s)}}
| rowspan=2 | {{para|spouse}} (will use {{tl|pluralize from text}})
|-
| {{para|spouses}}
|-
| {{para|nationality}} || remove
|}
</syntaxhighlight>

How the <code>#</code> row above works:
{| class="wikitable"
! Article has !! Bot changes it to
|-
| <code>termstart</code> || <code>term_start</code>
|-
| <code>termstart2</code> || <code>term_start2</code>
|-
| <code>termstart12</code> || <code>term_start12</code>
|-
| <code>termstarts</code> || ''no change: # only stands for a number''
|}

== Before you save ==
Check that:
* the table has a caption line, starting <code>|+</code>, straight after the <code>{|</code> line, naming the template
* the old names are in the first column and the new names in the second
* each row has one new name, or <code>remove</code>
* a <code>#</code> is in both names or in neither
* any example tables you wrote in a discussion on this page are inside <code><nowiki><syntaxhighlight lang="wikitext"> ... </syntaxhighlight></nowiki></code>. '''If they aren't, the bot will obey them.'''

== Checking your rules ==
After the bot's next daily run, look at [[User:ParamBot/Report]].
* '''Rules page problems''' lists anything the bot couldn't use and says how to fix it: for example a table with no caption, or a rename to a name the template doesn't accept. Fix those on this page.
* A '''Notes''' entry saying the template "still accepts" an old name is normal: nothing is broken yet, so the rule waits. If you meant the row the other way round, swap its two names.
* '''Needs human review''' lists articles where the old and the new parameter are both filled in with different values. The bot leaves those alone. Fix them by hand.

The bot checks every table on every run, so you don't have to wait for an article to need your rule before finding a mistake.

'''Want to see your rules in action?''' Put an infobox that uses the old names in your sandbox, and ask the bot operator on [[User talk:ParamBot]] to preview it. The bot shows what it would change without editing anything. It never edits sandboxes or anything else outside articles.

== What the bot does ==
{| class="wikitable"
! If the article has the old parameter… !! …and the new parameter is !! The bot
|-
| filled in || missing || renames the old parameter to the new name
|-
| filled in || there but empty || moves the value into the new parameter and deletes the old one
|-
| filled in || filled in with the same value || deletes the old one
|-
| filled in || filled in with a different value || does nothing and lists the article under ''Needs human review'', unless the row says <code>merge</code> ([[#If both parameters are filled in|see below]])
|-
| empty || anything || nothing, because an empty old parameter isn't breaking anything. (If the bot is editing the article anyway, it tidies these up too.)
|}

The bot also:
* only edits articles (main namespace)
* keeps the page's layout, including lined-up <code>=</code> signs
* won't edit an article again within 30 days of its last edit there, in case someone put the old parameter back on purpose. It lists the article under ''Not edited'' instead.
* stays off any article with {{tlx|bots|deny{{=}}ParamBot}} or {{tlx|nobots}}
* ignores a template's rules entirely if it can't read the template's list of accepted parameters. This is reported under ''Rules page problems''.

== If both parameters are filled in ==
By default, when an article has the old and the new parameter filled in with different values, the bot leaves it for a human. To merge them instead, add a third column headed <code>If both are set</code> and write <code>merge</code> in the rows that should be merged. The bot then adds the old value to the end of the new one, on a new line.

'''Only merge lists''', such as schools or subsidiaries. Never merge things like coordinates, numbers, dates or map names: two of those in one parameter breaks the infobox.

<syntaxhighlight lang="wikitext">
{| class="wikitable"
|+ {{tl|Infobox person}}
! Old parameter !! New parameter !! If both are set
|-
| {{para|alma_mater}} || {{para|education}} || merge
|-
| {{para|other_name}} || {{para|other_names}} ||
|}
</syntaxhighlight>

== A template with an unusual category ==
The bot watches the category "Pages using ''template'' with unknown parameters", with the template's name starting with a small letter (for example "Pages using infobox settlement with unknown parameters"). If a template uses a different category, put a link to it in the caption. To find a template's category, search its source for <code>with unknown parameters</code>.

<syntaxhighlight lang="wikitext">
{| class="wikitable"
|+ {{tl|Infobox foo}} watches [[:Category:Pages using infobox foo with bad parameters]]
! Old parameter !! New parameter
|-
| {{para|oldname}} || {{para|newname}}
|}
</syntaxhighlight>

Keep the colon before "Category". Without it, this page would be added to the category.

== The one-line format ==
Lines in the format of [[WP:AWB/RTP]] also work, and <code>#</code> means a number in them too:
<syntaxhighlight lang="wikitext">
* <code>{{AWB rename template parameter|Infobox officeholder|termstart#|term_start#}}</code>
</syntaxhighlight>
The bot watches the standard category for these, and they can't say <code>merge</code>.

== Common mistakes ==
{| class="wikitable"
! Mistake !! What happens !! Fix
|-
| No caption line || The bot ignores the table. If the names are written with <code><nowiki>{{para}}</nowiki></code>, the report says so. || Add <code><nowiki>|+ {{tl|Template name}}</nowiki></code> straight after <code>{|</code>
|-
| Old and new columns swapped || The rules never do anything, because the template accepts the "old" names. The report's ''Notes'' say so. || Swap the columns
|-
| Two new names in one row || The row is ignored and reported. || One new name per row
|-
| An empty new-name cell || The row is ignored and reported. || Write the new name, or <code>remove</code>
|-
| <code>#</code> in only one of the names || The row is ignored and reported. || Use <code>#</code> in both names or in neither
|-
| Several names as plain text: <code>a, b</code> || The row is ignored and reported. || Write each name as <code><nowiki>{{para|name}}</nowiki></code>
|-
| A note in a cell without <code><nowiki>{{para}}</nowiki></code>, such as <code>imagesize (typo)</code> || The note becomes part of the name. A new name like that is reported; an old one silently never matches. || Write the name as <code><nowiki>{{para|imagesize}}</nowiki></code>
|-
| The ''If both are set'' column says something other than <code>merge</code> || Reported, and treated as empty. || Write <code>merge</code> or leave it empty
|-
| Wrong capitals, such as <code>Imagesize</code> || Nothing happens. || Copy names exactly from the template
|-
| An example table in a discussion on this page, outside <code><nowiki><syntaxhighlight></nowiki></code> || '''The bot obeys it.''' || Put examples inside <code><nowiki><syntaxhighlight lang="wikitext"></nowiki></code>
|}

== If something goes wrong ==
* '''One bad edit:''' revert it and say what happened on [[User talk:ParamBot]]. The bot won't edit that article again for 30 days.
* '''Keep the bot off one article for good:''' add {{tlx|bots|deny{{=}}ParamBot}} to the article.
* '''The bot is misbehaving:''' change [[User:ParamBot/Run]] to <code>no</code>. The bot checks it before every edit, so it stops straight away, even in the middle of a run.
* '''The report starts with an ''Errors'' section:''' the last run didn't finish. Tell the bot operator.
